title: Bluefield deployment guide - bare metal & vSphere prototype
body:
Purpose:
This is a working prototype guide for field deployment of the ‘Bluefield’ on-prem Kubernetes footprint. Focus: mixed rack deployment where some nodes are bare metal and some are vSphere guests. Objective: a predictable, repeatable sequence that field engineers can run with a single terraform/tftp artifact bundle and a small set of ad-hoc commands.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target cluster size: 3 control-plane, 6-12 workers per rack (scales across racks).
- Hardware: commodity dual-socket servers (X86_64), each with IPMI/BMC or iLO.
- vSphere hosts: current customers may prefer VMs for some worker roles.
- Network: two physical networks available: mgmt (out-of-band), pod/tenant network (data).
- Storage: local NVMe for ephemeral workloads, optionally NFS/Ceph for PVs (note: PV provisioning is out of scope for first boot).
- Airgapped installs supported: bring-your-own container registry + offline terraform modules.

High-level flow (one-pass):
1) Rack-sweep inventory: confirm serial numbers, IPMI access, NIC mapping (documented in rack manifest).
2) Seed provisioning image: iPXE image + initrd on tftp/http server (or vSphere template for guests).
3) Terraform stage 0: create network objects, DHCP reservations for nodes, bootstrap VMs (for vSphere workers) and a small bastion VM used by field engineers.
4) Node imaging: bulk iPXE -> ubuntu-kernel+initramfs -> cloud-init from local metadata service.
5) Cluster bootstrap: run kubeadm-like controller bootstrap (we use our internal operatorless sequence; steps below).
6) Post-join tasks: telemetry agent, nvme-prep, localstorageclass marker, and remote logging forwarder.
7) Canary workload and health checks (telemetry-first).

Preflight checklist (quick):
- Rack manifest CSV present in /deploy/manifests/bluefield-rack-<id>.csv
- IPMI creds validated and accessible from ops-bastion
- TFTP/HTTP image server reachable from BMC network
- Terraform state bucket writable (or local state file in airgap)
- Time sync: NTP/chrony reachable or set on nodes via cloud-init
- KMS access for cluster secrets (customer-supplied) or KMS stub for offline test

Inventory and node-flavor matrix (example):
- controller-1..3: 2x A100-like, 512GB RAM (control only), NVMe 1TB
- worker-general-1..8: 1x A10G-like, 256GB RAM, NVMe 2TB
- worker-vm-1..4 (vSphere): 2 vCPU/16GB each for burst workloads
Note: real deployments will vary; keep mapping in terraform variables under node_map.

Network notes and gotchas:
- Avoid hairpinning management and data networks on the same switch VLANs during imaging; some POD-CNI probes fail if growth network is blackholed.
- Use deterministic MAC->IP mapping in DHCP (lease reservations) to make terraform idempotent across reboots.
- If using overlay (calico/flannel), pre-seed MTU and route leak rules in CNI conf via cloud-init.

IPMI and vSphere quick recipes:
- IPMI: bulk wipe (ipmitool chassis bootdev pxe), set boot order, trigger cold-boot -> monitor SOL log for u-boot/kernel messages.
- vSphere: import prebuilt template (ubuntu-automation-template) and clone with customization spec (static IP via terraform).
- Tip: maintain a small checksum file on templates to detect drift (template-checksum.txt) and fail early if wrong.

Terraform module notes (implementation sketch):
- module/bluefield-network: creates DHCP reservations (or updates local DHCP server config), creates portgroups for mgmt/data, and writes DNS A records to the internal DNS API.
- module/bluefield-ipmi: ipmi provider wrapper for lifecycle (power_on, set_bootpxe, remote_console_url output)
- module/bluefield-vsphere: lazy-clone template with per-VM customization, tags VM with cluster and rack metadata.
- idempotency: each module exports a stable resource id label (node_id) derived from rack+unit to allow safe reapply.
- variable strategy: keep node_map as a list of objects in TF var (but inside our repo this is YAML rendered to JSON for TF).

Bootstrapping sequence (detailed):
- Stage A (bastion + metadata): bring up ops-bastion, local metadata service (mini-http that serves cloud-init/user-data templates), and registry mirror (if airgap).
- Stage B (image nodes): kick nodes to network boot -> cloud-init pulls bootstrap script from metadata service -> installs container runtime + kube-binary and writes /opt/redwood/bootstrap/phase1.done
- Stage C (controller election): first controller runs init-controller.sh which provisions CA, writes join tokens to KMS or local sealed secret, and announces via etcd-boot-signal in S3-like object store.
- Stage D (workers join): workers use sealed join token and join control-plane endpoints (LB or direct, depending on config).
- Stage E (post-config): apply RBAC, storageclass, node-labels, taints, and health probes.

Upgrade plan (in-place rolling, rack-aware):
- Strategy: control-plane first (one at a time), then workers in rack-sweep batches (prefer 10-30% of workers concurrently).
- Canary: maintain a canary pool of nodes in a designated rack to test kernel/CRI and kubelet changes.
- Rollback: snapshot pv-metadata (if any), drain node, run upgrade binary, if fail then re-provision from image snapshot (we keep golden images in S3 or on USB in field).
- Terraform during upgrade: avoid re-creating compute resources; use taint/unset lifecycle prevent_destroy for controller nodes to reduce accidental re-provisioning.

Observability & telemetry-first checks (critical):
- Local prometheus-lite + pushgateway that forwards to main telemetry. On first boot register node heartbeat to central console within 10 minutes.
- Health probes we check before marking node healthy: kubelet status, containerd running, IPVS/netfilter rules, persistentlocalstorage marker.

Runbook snippets (commands for field engineer):
- Force PXE boot via IPMI: ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U <user> -P <pass> chassis bootdev pxe && ipmitool -I lanplus -H <bmc> -U <user> -P <pass> chassis power cycle
- Check bootstrap logs (ops-bastion): ssh ops@bastion tail -f /var/log/bluefield/bootstrap-<node>.log

Open questions / TODOs (for followups):
- How to integrate customer KMS with sealed-secrets in strict airgap (design ticket RDW-2379).
- Validate behavior when switch ACL blocks DHCP renewal during image -> observed intermittent CNI failures.
- Decide on pv reclaim policy for local NVMe (WIP: use local-storage operator vs CSI).

Notes to self / field tips:
- Always copy the rack-manifest to local USB before customs site handover.
- Keep an emergency re-image USB with kernel+initramfs for sites with flaky TFTP.
- Tag VM and baremetal nodes with the same cluster and rack metadata so our console shows unified topology.

Appendix: quick links and references:
- Template repo: git@github.com:redwood/infra-templates.git#bluefield
- TF module PR: https://git.internal.redwood/infra/terraform-modules/pull/542
- Related ticket: RDW-2315 (field deploy pilot)
- Confluence sketch: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/bluefield-deploy-notes

Status: prototype. This doc is intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive — aim is to get a reproducible field pass. After first two rack pilots, tighten up terraform variable surface and convert the brittle shell scripts into a small Go binary for join orchestration.

End of doc.
